newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria holds "promising" oil talks with US firms.
newsitem.headline: Algeria holds "promising" oil talks with US firms.

text.p: Algeria's state-owned oil and gas company Sonatrach said on Thursday it was holding "promising" talks with U.S. companies interested in partnership deals in prospecting for oil and in production.

A Sonatrach spokesman said a U.S. delegation which included general managers of Marathon International Petroleum and Marathon Power and U.S. Steel recently visited the Annaba steel complex and Msila power station.

"We presented a concrete proposals to the U.S. delegation for a partnership in the field of oil prospecting and production. What we can say at this stage is the continuing talks are promising," the spokesman said.
At Annaba, pipeline output from the Alfa-Tubes firm is devoted mainly to Sonatrach and domestic companies, he said.
The U.S. delegation also showed interest in an Algerian offer of partnership in the electricity and steel sectors.
"The talks, which we can say are very constructive, will continue in future to set up a framework of solid partnership between U.S. Marathon group and Algerian companies," he added.

According to press reports, the delegation also held talks with Energy Minister Amar Makhloufi on Tuesday on partnership opportunities with Sonatrach and Sonelgaz, the state electricity and gas corporation.
